correctness.rationale: On the cyclic shift module F_p[z]/(z^L-1) the map is triangular with diagonal 1,z,...,z. For L=dq, q=p^a, extension to a splitting field yields local z=lambda+b with b^q=0 at each dth root. The presence of every dth root for m>=1 gives prime-to-p order exactly d by the semisimple/unipotent decomposition. At lambda=1 put N=A-I. For k=p^e, N^k on column zero has coefficient (-1)^j binom(k-1,j-1)b^(k-j) in row j<=k: the first step must leave coordinate zero. The binomial coefficients are all units modulo p by Lucas, so row min(k,m) shows nonzero for k<m+q. For k>=m+q all such terms vanish; in positive columns Frobenius on bI-J kills all entries. On lambda!=1, B-I for the positive-index block is invertible, so the column coupling splits off and B^(dp^e)=I for k>=m+q. Raising a nontrivial p-group element to d coprime to p cannot erase the lower-bound obstruction. Thus the exact cutoff holds also when p divides L, including L=1, with m=0 identity. Compatible triangular inverses give the inverse-limit map, and finite order would bound all quotient orders. An independent direct iteration of every unit input (`python3 /workspace/reproduce.py`) verified the first identity time in 72 parameter triples, including m=0, mixed d and q, and powers of p. The frozen CHECK_OUTPUT.txt is recorded evidence only.
